chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that Satan's authority (sultan) is not absolute but conditional upon human voluntary submission, a key distinction in Shia theology that preserves free will against determinism. This narration underscores that while Shaytan has power over those who heed him, he holds no dominion over the sincere servants of Allah, reinforcing the concept of *wilayah* and spiritual autonomy.
